pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing items are 0 and the CHECK rejects 2.
src/index.js defaults view to open; 'AC-2' test covers / and ?view=open with id order.
'AC-3' test marks 3,1 done and expects ['✓ First item','✓ Third item'] in id order.
'AC-4' test checks all items, id order, ✓ only on done.
'AC-5' test asserts exact nav HTML for each view and for '/'; the current view is a <strong>, not a link.
'AC-6' test checks 400 and no <li> for Open, closed, empty and __proto__; Object.hasOwn guards the lookup.
'AC-7' test covers Nothing open, Nothing done yet, and No items yet. in all views when the table is empty.
traffic/routes.json lists both routes; 'AC-8' test checks them with arrayContaining. The traffic worker passes routes to app.fetch.

findings.what: The 'Follow-up edits' commit (dcb868f) loosened the synthetic-traffic test. `expect(app.seen.map(s=>s.path)).toEqual(["/healthz", ...ROUTES])` became `.toBeDefined()`, which can never fail. The test no longer checks that traffic hits /healthz and every listed route, including the new ?view routes. The spec does not justify this, and the PR claims 'Tests deleted or loosened: none'.
findings.fix: Restore the `toEqual(["/healthz", ...ROUTES])` assertion. The fake app now records pathname+search, so it will pass.

findings.what: The PR body says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but the final commit weakened a traffic assertion to toBeDefined(). The claim is false.
findings.fix: Fix the test and keep the claim accurate, or state the loosening in the PR.

findings.what: The README does not mention that any other view value answers 400, or that the synthetic-traffic route check now accepts queries.
findings.fix: Add one line on the 400 for an unknown view.

lenses.note: The spec exists and its decisions (open by default, query parameter) are followed. Nothing beyond the ask except the traffic-config check relaxation, which AC-8 requires.
All 8 AC items are implemented and named by tests, and every States row has a test. The only gap is the loosened traffic test.
npm test could not run here (vitest is not installed). By reading, test/done.test.js is solid. The traffic.test.js assertion was weakened to toBeDefined().
The README is updated for the views; the 400 case is not documented.
The implementation is correct, SQL is not built from user input, and unknown views are rejected through a hasOwn allowlist.
The view value is allowlisted, titles are HTML-escaped, and no injection path is visible.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no UI files or styling; there is no design surface to review beyond the nav markup checked in the tests.
No browser or UI flow was available; the behaviour is covered by the HTTP-level tests.
The 'none loosened' claim is false because of the follow-up commit. The title is under 72 characters.
